INTEGRATION STEP for Product Oracle v1. Read docs/v1-plan.md in full first. Lanes A (members), B2a/B2b (connectors) are already on main. The other lanes' work is on branches of origin: lane/k-connections, lane/b1-sources, lane/c-baseline, lane/f-templates, lane/d1-mcp, lane/d2-mcp-oauth, lane/e-runs (fetch them with git fetch origin 'refs/heads/lane/*:refs/remotes/origin/lane/*'). Each was built in parallel from an older main, and none was tested together.

1. Merge them into this branch in this order: k-connections, b1-sources, c-baseline, f-templates, d1-mcp, d2-mcp-oauth, e-runs. Resolve every conflict by keeping both lanes' intent: route registration in api/oracle/main.py, the generated web/lib/api (regenerate with `make openapi`, never hand-merge it), shared web navigation and components, and any duplicated helpers (B1 and K both read connection credentials: keep K's connections.service.get_credential and make B1 call it). Migrations: 0001-0003 on main, 0004 from d2-mcp-oauth; there must be one linear chain.
2. Wire the lanes together where each one left a hook: register D2's OAuth access-token verifier with D1's oracle.mcp.auth registry; make D1's curated search tool return B1's confidence; make E's runs ingest a segment's baseline.yaml artifact through C's YAML import (locks respected, proposals created); make F's priorities read C's evidence confidence.
3. Run everything: the full API suite against Postgres (ORACLE_TEST_DATABASE_URL), ruff check and ruff format --check, `make openapi` (commit the result), web lint, tsc, build, the Playwright mock suite, and `make e2e` if Postgres and Chromium are available. Fix what fails. If Chromium cannot start here, say so plainly; CI runs it.
4. Write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/integrate-report.md: conflicts and how each was resolved, wiring done, test results with counts, anything not verified.
Product Oracle words only: one company's Oracle, its users and their roles; never 'workspace'. Never touch .github/. Commit your work.

CLAUDE ACCOUNT POOL for Product Oracle v1. Read docs/v1-plan.md section 'Claude accounts' and docs/questions.md row P3b first; they are the spec. Oracle's own Claude calls run on a pool of Claude accounts managed like a mature account pool: states available | paused | draining | reauth_required, quota windows five_hour and seven_day (utilisation 0-1, resets_at, observed_at), holders, most-headroom choice. This replaces the per-user Claude plan that Lane K built in api/oracle/llm/ and its Claude card on Settings > Connections (data connections stay per user and untouched).

Build:
1. Migration 0005 (down_revision 0004) and models: llm_accounts (tenant-scoped; label unique per company, matching ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,38}[a-z0-9])?$; provider 'anthropic'; state; reason; state_before_reauth; windows JSONB; observed_at; credential ciphertext via oracle.crypto with auth kind setup_token | oauth_login; token_expires_at; last_refresh_at; added_by; last_assigned_at) and llm_holds (account, assignment id, purpose, user, started_at, expires_at, released_at, outcome).
2. Adding (owner): paste a `claude setup-token` value, or Claude Code's saved login JSON with a refresh token (with or without its claudeAiOauth wrapper); validate by a one-turn headless call; Oracle is the single writer that refreshes oauth_login credentials (save the new pair before using the new access token; a 400/401/invalid_grant marks reauth_required and keeps the previous state for recovery). No browser sign-in flow.
3. Calls: llm.complete(...) takes a hold on the chosen account, runs the call through Claude Code headless (claude-agent-sdk or `claude -p --output-format stream-json`) with CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set for that call only, records each rate_limit_event (rateLimitType, utilization, resetsAt; a rejection without utilisation counts as full) as a reading merged per window (older readings discarded), and releases the hold. Choice: available accounts with headroom >= 0.15 (headroom = minimum remaining across windows; a reading older than 30 minutes counts half; never read counts as full), then fewest holders, then label. None free: raise a clear error naming the next reset; never fall back silently. Draining: running holds finish at their turn boundary and new calls go elsewhere. Keep the Anthropic API key path from Lane K as an explicit, separate option.
4. API (owner for changes, approver+ to read): list with quota marks, add, PUT state {state, reason}, refresh now, DELETE (type-the-label confirmation in the UI), holders and history.
5. UI: Settings > Claude accounts: columns ACCOUNT | 5H USED | 7D USED | CLEARS | STATE with the marks: a measured value as N%, a stale one as ~N%, never measured as an em dash (never 0%); CLEARS = time until the binding window (least remaining) resets, 'cleared' once it has, ~ when based on a stale reading. Detail pane with holders and history, actions add / pause / resume / drain / refresh / remove.
6. Tests: choice policy (headroom, stale halving, unread, ties), state transitions, drain, reauth detection and recovery, refresh write order, readings merge, never-0 display, role checks, Playwright mock test for the page.
Run the full API suite, ruff, make openapi, web lint/tsc/build, Playwright mock tests. Commit. Write $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/claude-accounts-report.md. Product Oracle words only; never touch .github/.
